newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian economy will not grow in 1997 - govt source.
newsitem.headline: Russian economy will not grow in 1997 - govt source.

text.p: The Russian economy will not grow in 1997, a senior government official said on Friday, but added it could expand by a rate of between two to three percent in 1998.
The Economy Ministry said Russia's gross domestic product, which has been declining steeply since the beginning of economic reforms, would stabilise in 1997.
"If you look over the course of the year (month-on-month) there will be growth, but year-on-year there will not be," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
"For now we cannot talk of growth, although stabilisation is definitely happening. But next year of course there will be growth," he said, forecasting a rise of two to three percent.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais last month predicted the economy would grow modestly this year, by between 0.5 and 2.5 percent.
And he has said repeatedly that Russia could look forward to an economic spurt next year.
But this week he suggested growth would be postponed until next year.
"The main task of the government must be to ensure that 1998 becomes the year of growth," Chubais told regional governors in the Siberian city of Krasnoyarsk.

Official figures show GDP grew 0.2 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997, but statisticians said an increase of this order could not be counted as proper economic growth, while analysts query the accuracy of the numbers themselves.

Economists say the State Statistics Committee changed the weighting given this year to the unofficial or "shadow" economy, which is widely acknowledged to be booming, in calculating GDP without making the same changes to last year's figures.
The committee says the figures will be reviewed as a matter of course, but denies it distorted the numbers to support government reforms, and says they will not change significantly after revision.
